title: I built a golf management sim with generative AI — the AI wrote the code, I did the playtesting
author: Manager-Games145
selftext:
I built Links Manager, a golf management sim — Football Manager meets golf. You run an academy: sign junior golfers, hire coaches, pick tournaments, manage the money, and chase majors across multi-season careers. Free browser demo (one full 26-week season), $5 full game on itch.io.
    
    The whole thing was built with generative AI. I started it in Manus, describing the game I wanted in prompts, then kept developing it with an AI coding assistant — new features, bug fixes, economy rebalancing, all through conversation. I don't write the code; I direct, playtest, and call out what's wrong.
    
    What the AI was genuinely good at:
    - Scaffolding fast — first playable version in days, not months
    - Grinding through fiddly logic: tournament settlement, tee times and pairings, save/load, playoffs
    - Iterating — I'd describe a bug in plain words, it'd fix it
    
    What needed a human:
    - Playtesting feel. The AI can't tell you majors are too easy to win (they were — I had the economy rebalanced) or that new players don't know what to do in the first 10 minutes
    - Taste calls — what's fun vs what's just complicated
    - Catching the subtle bugs only a player notices
    
    Demo: https://tomhs183.itch.io/links-manager-demo
    Full game: https://tomhs183.itch.io/links-manager
    
    Happy to answer anything on the workflow — prompting approach, how I verify AI-written game logic, whatever's useful.
